name: Hillman Solutions Corp
business: Distributes fasteners, hardware, protective gear and robotic key-duplication kiosks to home centers, hardware stores and mass merchants across North America.

events.what: Definitive agreement to acquire Kanebridge (industrial fastener distributor, about $65M LTM revenue, $30M adjusted EBITDA) for $315M; about $2M cost synergies; expected close around start of Q4 2026; pending
Acquisitions closed: Campbell Chain & Fittings and Delaney Hardware (combined about $30M 2026 net sales)
events.source: document_id 196291 (Q1 2026 call: closed subsequent to quarter end; exact close date not stated, 2026-04-28 is the call date)

events.what: First-ever Investor Day: 2030 targets of $2.5B net sales, 8% to 12% annual growth, low double-digit adjusted EBITDA CAGR, leverage 2.5x or below
OUTSIDE WINDOW: CEO and President appointed (internal, ex COO, ex Stanley Black & Decker); predecessor Douglas Cahill to Executive Chairman

next_event.source: Investor Day already held 2026-03-19 (document_id 142671). No further investor day or margin framework update announced. Next dated item is the Kanebridge close, guided 'around the start of the fourth quarter' 2026 (document_id 128949).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Investor Day targets are a 2030 net sales level ($2.5B) and an adjusted EBITDA growth rate (low double-digit CAGR), not a margin. Implied 2030 margin is 17.7% at a 10% EBITDA CAGR and 19.4% at 12% from the FY2025 base of $275.3M (derived, not stated). The only explicit margin number (20% 'not out of the question', no year) came from IR, not the CEO or CFO, in February 2025.

statements.quote: Over the next five years, we are confident we will grow Hillman's total net sales to $2.5 billion in 2030. To reach this number, we are targeting 8%-12% growth per year, which will be driven by core performance, new business wins, both at retail and in the pro channel, and M&A. During the same timeline, our goal is to grow adjusted EBITDA at a low double-digit CAGR, maintain a healthy balance sheet while targeting leverage of 2.5x or below, and drive our return on invested capital into the high teens.
statements.speaker: Jon Michael Adinolfi
statements.doc_title: Hillman Solutions Corp Q1 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: Adjusted EBITDA to net sales margin during the quarter totaled 17.4%, down 130 basis points from a year ago, improving meaningfully from 13.5% in the first quarter.
statements.speaker: Rocky Kraft
statements.doc_title: Hillman Solutions Corp Q2 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: So again, we feel really confident that with that business back to growth, I'm not going to predict the year, but a 20% EBITDA rate is not out of the question when you think about that mix shift.
statements.speaker: Michael Koehler
statements.doc_title: Hillman Solutions Corp Q4 2024 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: No stated margin target. Uses the implied 2030 margin from Investor Day targets at the low end (FY2025 adjusted EBITDA $275.3M grown 10% a year to 2030 over $2.5B sales = 17.74%) minus VA consensus FY2030 EBITDA margin 19.08% = -135 bps; at a 12% CAGR the implied margin is 19.41%, +33 bps. The street already models more margin than management's targets imply; the upside in the targets is revenue and M&A (consensus FY2030 revenue $2.06B vs $2.5B target). Calendar FY labels (December FYE).
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (summary, FY2026 to FY2030)

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], adjusted EBITDA margin YoY per CFO Kraft: Q1 13.5% (doc 196291), Q2 17.4% (doc 128949); driven by high-cost tariffed inventory. Sequential recovery from 13.5% to 17.4%. LTM 17.02% uses VA actuals Q3 2025 to Q1 2026 plus company-reported Q2 2026 ($442.3M, $77.1M).

verdict: Weak archetype match despite 7/10: cheapest in its own history with a pending $315M deal, but the CEO is 21 months in, there is no margin target, and the street already sits above implied 2030 margin.
open_questions: Does the Kanebridge close (around Q4 2026 start) come with a margin or synergy framework beyond the $2M sourcing figure?
Is the Q1 to Q2 2026 margin recovery from tariffed inventory durable enough to get back above the 2025 level of 17.7%?
Will management convert the 2030 EBITDA CAGR into an explicit margin target, given IR's earlier 20% comment?
